Let x = number of units of gadget A produced and y = number of units of gadget B produced.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 30x + 20y\)

Constraints:
Foundry time (available 60 hr): \(10x + 6y \le 60\)
Machine-shop time (available 35 hr): \(5x + 4y \le 35\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 30x + 20y\)
subject to
\(10x + 6y \le 60\)
\(5x + 4y \le 35\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Let x = number of units of fodder 1 and y = number of units of fodder 2 in the ration.

Objective (minimize cost):
\(Z = 3x + 2y\)

Constraints (each animal's ration must meet the minimum nutrient requirement):
Nutrient A (need 14): \(2x + y \ge 14\)
Nutrient B (need 22): \(2x + 3y \ge 22\)
Nutrient C (need 1): \(x + y \ge 1\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Minimize \(Z = 3x + 2y\)
subject to
\(2x + y \ge 14\)
\(2x + 3y \ge 22\)
\(x + y \ge 1\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Let x = number of units of food A and y = number of units of food B in the weekly diet.

Objective (minimize cost):
\(Z = 4.5x + 3.5y\)

Constraints (diet must meet the minimum requirements):
Fats (need 18): \(4x + 6y \ge 18\)
Carbohydrates (need 28): \(14x + 12y \ge 28\)
Proteins (need 14): \(8x + 8y \ge 14\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Minimize \(Z = 4.5x + 3.5y\)
subject to
\(4x + 6y \ge 18\)
\(14x + 12y \ge 28\)
\(8x + 8y \ge 14\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Let x = distance (in km) travelled at the speed of 60 km/hr and y = distance (in km) travelled at the speed of 90 km/hr.

Objective (maximize the distance travelled):
\(Z = x + y\)

Constraints:
Petrol budget (Rs. 5 per km at 60 km/hr, Rs. 8 per km at 90 km/hr, at most Rs. 600): \(5x + 8y \le 600\)
Time available (time = distance / speed, at most 1 hour): \(\dfrac{x}{60} + \dfrac{y}{90} \le 1\), i.e. \(3x + 2y \le 180\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = x + y\)
subject to
\(5x + 8y \le 600\)
\(3x + 2y \le 180\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Let x = weight (in kg) of cement and y = weight (in kg) of sand used in one concrete brick.

Objective (minimize cost):
\(Z = 20x + 6y\)

Constraints:
Brick weight at least 5 kg: \(x + y \ge 5\)
Cement at least 4 kg: \(x \ge 4\)
Sand not more than 2 kg: \(y \le 2\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Minimize \(Z = 20x + 6y\)
subject to
\(x + y \ge 5\)
\(x \ge 4\)
\(y \le 2\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Let x = number of mixers and y = number of food processors produced per week.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 2000x + 3000y\)

Constraints (weekly machine hours):
Machine A (available 36 hr): \(3x + 3y \le 36\)
Machine B (available 50 hr): \(5x + 2y \le 50\)
Machine C (available 60 hr): \(2x + 6y \le 60\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 2000x + 3000y\)
subject to
\(3x + 3y \le 36\)
\(5x + 2y \le 50\)
\(2x + 6y \le 60\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(3x + 3y = 36\) (i.e. \(x + y = 12\)), \(5x + 2y = 50\) and \(2x + 6y = 60\) (i.e. \(x + 3y = 30\)).

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((0,0)\)
\((10,0)\), the x-intercept of \(5x + 2y = 50\)
\(\left(\dfrac{26}{3}, \dfrac{10}{3}\right)\), the intersection of \(5x + 2y = 50\) and \(x + y = 12\): from \(y = 12 - x\), \(5x + 2(12 - x) = 50\) gives \(3x = 26\)
\((3,9)\), the intersection of \(x + y = 12\) and \(x + 3y = 30\): subtracting gives \(2y = 18\), \(y = 9\), \(x = 3\)
\((0,10)\), the y-intercept of \(x + 3y = 30\)

| Corner point | \(Z = 2000x + 3000y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((10,0)\) | \(20000\) |
| \(\left(\dfrac{26}{3}, \dfrac{10}{3}\right)\) | \(\dfrac{82000}{3} \approx 27333.33\) |
| \((3,9)\) | \(33000\) |
| \((0,10)\) | \(30000\) |

The maximum value is \(Z = 33000\) at \((x, y) = (3, 9)\).

Hence produce 3 mixers and 9 food processors for a maximum profit of Rs. 33000.

Let x = number of units of compound I and y = number of units of compound II mixed.

Objective (minimize cost):
\(Z = 800x + 640y\)

Constraints (chemical must contain at least the stated amount of each element):
Element A (at least 16 litres): \(4x + 2y \ge 16\), i.e. \(2x + y \ge 8\)
Element B (at least 24 litres): \(12x + 2y \ge 24\), i.e. \(6x + y \ge 12\)
Element C (at least 18 litres): \(2x + 6y \ge 18\), i.e. \(x + 3y \ge 9\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Minimize \(Z = 800x + 640y\)
subject to
\(4x + 2y \ge 16\)
\(12x + 2y \ge 24\)
\(2x + 6y \ge 18\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(4x + 2y = 16\) (i.e. \(2x + y = 8\)), \(12x + 2y = 24\) (i.e. \(6x + y = 12\)) and \(2x + 6y = 18\) (i.e. \(x + 3y = 9\)). The feasible region is unbounded.

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((9,0)\), the x-intercept of \(x + 3y = 9\) (satisfies \(2x + y = 18 \ge 8\) and \(6x + y = 54 \ge 12\))
\((3,2)\), the intersection of \(x + 3y = 9\) and \(2x + y = 8\): from \(x = 9 - 3y\), \(2(9 - 3y) + y = 8\) gives \(-5y = -10\), \(y = 2\), \(x = 3\)
\((1,6)\), the intersection of \(2x + y = 8\) and \(6x + y = 12\): subtracting gives \(4x = 4\), \(x = 1\), \(y = 6\)
\((0,12)\), the y-intercept of \(6x + y = 12\)

| Corner point | \(Z = 800x + 640y\) |
|---|---|
| \((9,0)\) | \(7200\) |
| \((3,2)\) | \(3680\) |
| \((1,6)\) | \(4640\) |
| \((0,12)\) | \(7680\) |

The minimum value is \(Z = 3680\) at \((x, y) = (3, 2)\).

Hence mix 3 units of compound I and 2 units of compound II for a minimum cost of Rs. 3680.

Let x = number of gift items of type A and y = number of gift items of type B made each month.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 75x + 125y\)

Constraints (monthly available hours):
Cutter's time (available 208 hr): \(4x + 2y \le 208\)
Finisher's time (available 152 hr): \(2x + 4y \le 152\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 75x + 125y\)
subject to
\(4x + 2y \le 208\)
\(2x + 4y \le 152\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(4x + 2y = 208\) (i.e. \(2x + y = 104\)) and \(2x + 4y = 152\) (i.e. \(x + 2y = 76\)).

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((0,0)\)
\((52,0)\), the x-intercept of \(2x + y = 104\)
\((44,16)\), the intersection of \(2x + y = 104\) and \(x + 2y = 76\): from \(y = 104 - 2x\), \(x + 2(104 - 2x) = 76\) gives \(-3x = -132\), \(x = 44\), \(y = 16\)
\((0,38)\), the y-intercept of \(x + 2y = 76\)

| Corner point | \(Z = 75x + 125y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((52,0)\) | \(3900\) |
| \((44,16)\) | \(5300\) |
| \((0,38)\) | \(4750\) |

The maximum value is \(Z = 5300\) at \((x, y) = (44, 16)\).

Hence make 44 gift items of type A and 16 of type B for a maximum profit of Rs. 5300.

Let x = number of units of product A and y = number of units of product B manufactured per working day.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 3x + 4y\)

Constraints (daily processing minutes):
Machine \(M_1\) (available 450 min): \(x + y \le 450\)
Machine \(M_2\) (available 600 min): \(2x + y \le 600\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 3x + 4y\)
subject to
\(x + y \le 450\)
\(2x + y \le 600\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(x + y = 450\) and \(2x + y = 600\).

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((0,0)\)
\((300,0)\), the x-intercept of \(2x + y = 600\)
\((150,300)\), the intersection of \(x + y = 450\) and \(2x + y = 600\): subtracting gives \(x = 150\), \(y = 300\)
\((0,450)\), the y-intercept of \(x + y = 450\)

| Corner point | \(Z = 3x + 4y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((300,0)\) | \(900\) |
| \((150,300)\) | \(1650\) |
| \((0,450)\) | \(1800\) |

The maximum value is \(Z = 1800\) at \((x, y) = (0, 450)\).

Hence manufacture 0 units of product A and 450 units of product B for a maximum profit of Rs. 1800.

Let x = number of units of item A and y = number of units of item B manufactured per month.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 20x + 30y\)

Constraints (monthly supply of components):
Motors (available 210): \(3x + 2y \le 210\)
Transformers (available 300): \(2x + 4y \le 300\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 20x + 30y\)
subject to
\(3x + 2y \le 210\)
\(2x + 4y \le 300\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(3x + 2y = 210\) and \(2x + 4y = 300\) (i.e. \(x + 2y = 150\)).

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((0,0)\)
\((70,0)\), the x-intercept of \(3x + 2y = 210\)
\((30,60)\), the intersection of \(3x + 2y = 210\) and \(x + 2y = 150\): subtracting gives \(2x = 60\), \(x = 30\), then \(30 + 2y = 150\) gives \(y = 60\)
\((0,75)\), the y-intercept of \(x + 2y = 150\)

| Corner point | \(Z = 20x + 30y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((70,0)\) | \(1400\) |
| \((30,60)\) | \(2400\) |
| \((0,75)\) | \(2250\) |

The maximum value is \(Z = 2400\) at \((x, y) = (30, 60)\).

Hence manufacture 30 units of item A and 60 units of item B for a maximum profit of Rs. 2400.

Let x = number of chairs and y = number of tables made.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 140x + 210y\)

Constraints (available machine hours):
Assembling (available 36 hr): \(3x + 3y \le 36\), i.e. \(x + y \le 12\)
Finishing (available 50 hr): \(5x + 2y \le 50\)
Polishing (available 60 hr): \(2x + 6y \le 60\), i.e. \(x + 3y \le 30\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 140x + 210y\)
subject to
\(x + y \le 12\)
\(5x + 2y \le 50\)
\(x + 3y \le 30\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The corner points of the feasible region are \((0,0)\), \((10,0)\), \(\left(\dfrac{26}{3},\ \dfrac{10}{3}\right)\), \((3,9)\) and \((0,10)\).

Evaluating \(Z = 140x + 210y\) at each:
\((0,0):\ Z = 0\)
\((10,0):\ Z = 1400\)
\(\left(\dfrac{26}{3},\dfrac{10}{3}\right):\ Z = \dfrac{5740}{3} \approx 1913.33\)
\((3,9):\ Z = 420 + 1890 = 2310\)
\((0,10):\ Z = 2100\)

The maximum value is \(Z = 2310\) at \((x, y) = (3, 9)\).

Hence the carpenter should make 3 chairs and 9 tables for a maximum profit of Rs. 2310.

Let x = number of bicycles and y = number of tricycles manufactured.

Objective (maximize profit):
\(Z = 180x + 220y\)

Constraints (available machine hours):
Machine A (available 120 hr): \(6x + 4y \le 120\), i.e. \(3x + 2y \le 60\)
Machine B (available 180 hr): \(3x + 10y \le 180\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Maximize \(Z = 180x + 220y\)
subject to
\(6x + 4y \le 120\)
\(3x + 10y \le 180\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(3x + 2y = 60\) and \(3x + 10y = 180\).

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((0,0)\)
\((20,0)\), the x-intercept of \(3x + 2y = 60\) (feasible, since \(3(20) + 10(0) = 60 \le 180\))
\((10,15)\), the intersection of \(3x + 2y = 60\) and \(3x + 10y = 180\): subtracting gives \(8y = 120\), so \(y = 15\), then \(3x + 30 = 60\) gives \(x = 10\)
\((0,18)\), the y-intercept of \(3x + 10y = 180\) (feasible, since \(3(0) + 2(18) = 36 \le 60\))

| Corner point | \(Z = 180x + 220y\) |
|---|---|
| \((0,0)\) | \(0\) |
| \((20,0)\) | \(3600\) |
| \((10,15)\) | \(5100\) |
| \((0,18)\) | \(3960\) |

The maximum value is \(Z = 5100\) at \((x, y) = (10, 15)\).

Hence the firm should manufacture 10 bicycles and 15 tricycles for a maximum profit of Rs. 5100.

Let x = number of units of chemical A and y = number of units of chemical B produced (in kg).

Objective (minimize cost):
\(Z = 4x + 6y\)

Constraints (minimum requirements of the ingredients):
Ingredient P (at least 80 units): \(x + 2y \ge 80\)
Ingredient Q (at least 75 units): \(3x + y \ge 75\)
Non-negativity: \(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

The complete L.P.P. is:
Minimize \(Z = 4x + 6y\)
subject to
\(x + 2y \ge 80\)
\(3x + y \ge 75\)
\(x \ge 0,\ y \ge 0\)

Graphical solution:
The boundary lines are \(x + 2y = 80\) and \(3x + y = 75\). Since the constraints are \(\ge\) type, the feasible region is unbounded (above the lines).

Corner points of the feasible region:
\((80,0)\), the x-intercept of \(x + 2y = 80\) (feasible, since \(3(80) + 0 = 240 \ge 75\))
\((14,33)\), the intersection of \(x + 2y = 80\) and \(3x + y = 75\): from the second line \(y = 75 - 3x\), so \(x + 2(75 - 3x) = 80\) gives \(-5x = -70\), \(x = 14\), \(y = 33\)
\((0,75)\), the y-intercept of \(3x + y = 75\) (feasible, since \(0 + 2(75) = 150 \ge 80\))

| Corner point | \(Z = 4x + 6y\) |
|---|---|
| \((80,0)\) | \(320\) |
| \((14,33)\) | \(254\) |
| \((0,75)\) | \(450\) |

Although the region is unbounded, drawing \(4x + 6y = 254\) shows no feasible point gives a smaller value, so the minimum value is \(Z = 254\) at \((x, y) = (14, 33)\).

Hence produce 14 units of chemical A and 33 units of chemical B for a minimum cost of Rs. 254.
